content: Ingredients Serves 2 250g rigatoni 250g brown mushrooms 150g baby spinach ½ red onion, finely diced (brunoise) 200ml double cream 3 tbsp pesto 30g Parmesan, grated 50ml olive oil Salt, pepper, and chilli flakes Method Bring a large pot of well-salted water to the boil. Sauté the onion in olive oil over medium heat until softened. Add the mushrooms and cook until lightly browned. Cook the rigatoni for 8 minutes until al dente. Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining. Add the cream to the mushroom pan and reduce by a third. Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the pesto on low heat. Add the drained pasta to the sauce with 2 tbsp of pasta water and the spinach. Toss until the spinach wilts. Serve topped with Parmesan and chilli flakes. Notes The pasta water is the key step — the starch thickens the sauce and rounds out the flavour. Don’t skip it.
description: Rigatoni al dente in a creamy mushroom and basil pesto sauce, finished with spinach and Parmesan.

Reserve a cup of pasta water before draining.
title: Rigatoni with Brown Mushrooms and Pesto

content: Ingredients Serves 3 3 chicken fillets, cut into bite-sized pieces 5 tbsp oil 1 tsp cumin seeds ½ tsp hing (asafoetida) 1 dried red chilli 1 onion, finely chopped 1 inch fresh ginger, grated 3 garlic cloves, grated 1 fresh green chilli, finely chopped 400g tin chopped tomatoes 3 tbsp natural yoghurt, whisked Fresh coriander, to garnish Spice paste ⅓ tsp turmeric 1 tsp cumin powder 1 tsp coriander powder ½ tsp chilli powder ¾ tsp salt 1 tsp garam masala 2 tbsp oil, to loosen Method Prep everything first. Mix the turmeric, cumin powder, coriander powder, chilli powder, salt, and garam masala with oil until the consistency of yoghurt. Have all other ingredients ready before you start cooking. Vaghar (tempering). Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds, hing, and dried red chilli and let them sizzle for 30 seconds. Fry the onion. Add the onion and fry until soft and golden. Add ginger, garlic, and chilli. Fry for 1 minute. Check the oil. You should see a little oil floating in the onion mixture — add more if needed. This matters for cooking the spice paste properly. Cook the spice paste. Turn the heat to high, add the paste, and stir constantly so it doesn’t stick. Cook until the oil begins to separate from the spices. Seal the chicken. Add the chicken and stir-fry on high heat to seal it and keep the juices in. Add the tomatoes. Once the chicken is mostly cooked through (cut a piece to check), add the chopped tomatoes a little at a time, keeping the heat high. Simmer. Once all the tomatoes are in, lower the heat, cover, and simmer until the chicken is cooked through. Taste and adjust spices as needed. Stir in the yoghurt. Turn the heat to low and add the yoghurt one tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly to prevent curdling. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve.
description: A dry, intensely spiced bhuna with a rich tomato and yoghurt base.
